title: Japan for Car Lovers — First Time, Full Throttle: 15 days across Tokyo, Osaka, Kyoto, Nagoya & back — JDM culture, ancient temples & family fun
description: This is the ultimate first-time Japan trip for a family that lives and breathes cars. You'll hunt JDM legends at Daikoku PA, stand where Toyota was born in Nagoya, go-kart through Tokyo's neon streets, and still have time for ancient temples, insane street food, and Golden Week festivals. From the Wangan highway to the bamboo groves of Arashiyama — every day is a new gear.

days.title: Touchdown Tokyo — Welcome to Japan
days.description: Land in Tokyo, get your bearings, and dive straight into the electric energy of Shinjuku and Shibuya. Your Japan adventure starts with neon lights, scramble crossings, and your first bowl of real ramen.

activities.name: Arrive & Set Up Base in Shinjuku
activities.description: Clear customs, grab your Suica IC card and pocket WiFi at the airport, then take the Narita Express or Limousine Bus to Shinjuku. Drop bags at your hotel and get oriented. Shake off the jet lag with a walk through Shinjuku's dizzying layers — from the towering skyscrapers of the west side to the intimate alleyways of Omoide Yokocho.

activities.name: Shibuya Scramble & First Night Vibes
activities.description: Take the train one stop to Shibuya and witness the famous Shibuya Scramble Crossing — up to 3,000 people crossing at once. The energy is unreal, especially at night.

days.title: Ancient Temples & Akihabara Car Shops
days.description: Start at Tokyo's oldest temple, then head to the electric town of Akihabara — where anime, electronics, and car culture shops collide.

activities.name: Senso-ji Temple & Nakamise Street
activities.description: Tokyo's oldest and most visited temple. Walk through the iconic Kaminarimon (Thunder Gate), browse the Nakamise shopping street for snacks and souvenirs.

activities.name: Akihabara — Electric Town & Car Culture
activities.description: Akihabara is famous for anime and electronics, but car lovers: browse die-cast car models, racing sim arcades, and automotive manga. Walk through Ueno Park for late cherry blossoms, then dive into the chaotic Ameyoko market for street food and deals.

activities.name: Tokyo Skytree at Sunset
activities.description: End the day at Japan's tallest structure (634m). The sunset views are breathtaking — on clear days you can see Mt. Fuji.

days.title: Odaiba — Cars, Tech & Tokyo Bay
days.description: Golden Week begins! Head to Odaiba for car heaven: Toyota showcase, teamLab Borderless, life-size Gundam, and the massive Super Autobacs auto parts store.

activities.name: Toyota MEGA WEB / Toyota City Showcase
activities.description: A car lover's dream — Toyota's massive showroom and museum. See concept cars, racing vehicles, and the History Garage with vintage JDM classics.

activities.name: Super Autobacs Tokyo Bay Shinonome
activities.description: The biggest auto parts store in Tokyo. Three floors: performance parts, car audio, wheels, JDM accessories, and a service center. One of the most mind-blowing art experiences on earth. Immersive digital art that reacts to your movement — waterfalls, flowers, and infinite mirrors.

activities.name: Rainbow Bridge Walk & Sunset
activities.description: Walk across the Rainbow Bridge at sunset. See the Statue of Liberty replica and Tokyo's skyline glittering across the bay.

days.title: Harajuku, Meiji Shrine & Go-Kart Tokyo
days.description: Serene Meiji Shrine, wild Harajuku fashion streets, then the ultimate — go-karting through Tokyo's streets in costume.

activities.name: Meiji Jingu Shrine
activities.description: Tokyo's most important Shinto shrine, hidden inside 170 acres of forest. Walk through massive torii gates and feel the calm — steps from Harajuku's chaos.

activities.name: Harajuku & Takeshita Street
activities.description: The epicenter of Japanese youth culture. Takeshita-dori is packed with colorful shops, crepe stands, and wild fashion.

activities.name: 🏎️ Go-Kart Street Tour — Tokyo
activities.description: THE car experience. Dress up in costume and drive go-karts through actual Tokyo streets — past Tokyo Tower, through Shibuya, under Rainbow Bridge.

days.title: Tsukiji Feast & Daikoku PA Night Meet
days.description: Morning: eat through Tsukiji Outer Market. Afternoon: upscale Ginza. Night: Daikoku PA, Japan's most legendary car meet where hundreds of modified JDM cars gather.

activities.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Crawl
activities.description: The outer market is still the beating heart of Tokyo's food scene. Wander the lanes eating fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, grilled seafood on sticks, and melon.

activities.name: Ginza District & Nissan Crossing
activities.description: Tokyo's most upscale shopping district. Car lovers: don't miss Nissan Crossing — Nissan's flagship showroom with concept cars and GT-R displays.

activities.name: 🏎️ Daikoku PA Night Car Meet
activities.description: This is IT. Daikoku PA is where Japan's car scene comes alive. Hundreds of modified cars: GT-Rs, Silvias, RX-7s, bosozoku vans, drift missiles, and pristine classics. Engine revs echo off the highway overpasses.

days.title: Shinkansen to Osaka — Street Food Capital
days.description: Board the bullet train to Osaka in 2.5 hours. Osaka is Japan's kitchen — tonight: Dotonbori, the most electric food street in the world.

activities.name: Shinkansen to Osaka
activities.description: Take the Tokaido Shinkansen from Tokyo Station to Shin-Osaka. Watch Japan's countryside and Mt. Fuji fly past at 300km/h.

activities.name: Shinsekai & Tsutenkaku Tower
activities.description: Osaka's retro entertainment district frozen in time from the 1950s. Colorful signs, kushikatsu shops everywhere, and the iconic Tsutenkaku Tower.

activities.name: Dotonbori Food Street Extravaganza
activities.description: Sensory overload of neon signs, giant mechanical crabs, and food stalls along the canal. Eat takoyaki, okonomiyaki, and gyoza until you can't move.

days.title: Osaka Castle, Markets & Wagyu Night
days.description: Explore Osaka's historic heart — the magnificent castle, Kuromon Market for fresh seafood, Den-Den Town for car hobby shops, and a splurge wagyu dinner.

activities.name: Osaka Castle & Nishinomaru Garden
activities.description: One of Japan's most iconic castles. The grounds are massive — moats, stone walls, and gardens. Inside, the museum covers Osaka's feudal history.

activities.name: Den-Den Town — Car Shops & Retro Games
activities.description: Osaka's version of Akihabara, less touristy with better car culture shops. Scale models, retro games, and automotive hobby stores. 600-meter covered shopping street. Boutiques, street fashion, and drugstores — great for families.

activities.name: Umeda Sky Building Sunset
activities.description: Two towers connected by a floating garden observatory 173m up. Night views of Osaka's sprawling lights are spectacular.

days.title: Kyoto Day Trip — Temples, Gates & Bamboo
days.description: Day trip to Kyoto — 15 minutes by Shinkansen from Osaka. Hit the three icons: Fushimi Inari's torii gates, Kinkaku-ji's golden pavilion, and Arashiyama's bamboo groves.

activities.name: Fushimi Inari Taisha — 10,000 Torii Gates
activities.description: Thousands of vermillion torii gates wind up a forested mountain. The full hike takes 2-3 hours, but even 30 minutes is breathtaking.

activities.name: Kinkaku-ji — The Golden Pavilion
activities.description: A Zen temple covered entirely in gold leaf, reflecting in its mirror pond. Looks even better in person. Quick 30-45 min visit but essential.

activities.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove & Monkey Park
activities.description: Walk through towering bamboo forest — another world. Climb to the Monkey Park where wild macaques roam with Kyoto as the backdrop.

activities.name: Return to Osaka
activities.description: Take the JR train back (30-45 min). You've earned a big dinner after a full day of temples.

days.title: Shinkansen to Nagoya — Toyota's Hometown
days.description: Children's Day! Head to Nagoya — the automotive heart of Japan. Toyota, Mitsubishi, and countless parts makers call this region home.

activities.name: Shinkansen to Nagoya
activities.description: Quick 50-minute bullet train from Shin-Osaka to Nagoya. Look for koinobori (carp streamers) flying for Children's Day.

activities.name: Osu Shopping District
activities.description: Nagoya's Akihabara meets Harajuku — covered arcade with retro vibes, anime shops, and car culture stores. Futuristic transit hub with glass 'Water Spaceship' roof. Adjacent is Japan's oldest TV tower.

activities.name: Sakae District Night Walk
activities.description: Nagoya's main entertainment district — department stores, izakaya, and nightlife. More relaxed than Tokyo.

days.title: Toyota Museum Day — Where Cars Were Born
days.description: The pilgrimage every car lover must make. The Toyota Museum traces how a loom maker became the world's biggest car company. Then Toyota City for the Kaikan Museum.

activities.name: 🏎️ Toyota Commemorative Museum of Industry and Technology
activities.description: Automotive Mecca. In Toyota's original 1911 factory — vintage cars, working engines, assembly line demos, and the Technoland play area for kids.

activities.name: 🏎️ Toyota Kaikan Museum — Toyota City
activities.description: Take the train to Toyota City (1 hour) for Toyota's corporate museum. Latest models, safety tech, hydrogen fuel cells, and racing vehicles.

activities.name: Atsuta Shrine & Hitsumabushi
activities.description: Visit one of Japan's most sacred Shinto shrines, then the city's most famous dish: hitsumabushi — grilled eel eaten three ways.

days.title: Nagoya Castle & the Fastest Train on Earth
days.description: Nagoya Castle's golden shachihoko, then the SCMAGLEV and Railway Park — Japan's train history including the world's fastest maglev (603 km/h). Perfect for a family that loves things that go fast.

activities.name: Nagoya Castle
activities.description: One of Japan's most important castles, famous for golden shachihoko roof ornaments. The reconstructed Honmaru Palace is a masterpiece of traditional architecture.

activities.name: SCMAGLEV and Railway Park
activities.description: JR Central's incredible train museum. Walk through retired Shinkansen, steam locomotives, and the actual maglev test vehicle that hit 603 km/h. The simulator experiences are a must.

activities.name: Farewell Nagoya Night
activities.description: Last evening in Nagoya — revisit your favorite food street or explore a new area. Consider the Noritake Garden (ceramics museum) if time allows.

days.title: Back to Tokyo — Toyosu & Roppongi Hills
days.description: Return to Tokyo by Shinkansen. Visit the new Toyosu Fish Market (where Tsukiji's inner market moved), then spend the evening at Roppongi Hills for art and city views.

activities.name: Shinkansen Back to Tokyo
activities.description: 1h40 on the Hikari from Nagoya back to Tokyo Station. Quick, comfortable, and scenic.

activities.name: Toyosu Fish Market
activities.description: The massive new fish market that replaced Tsukiji's inner market. Watch the famous tuna auction (from a viewing gallery), browse the wholesale area, and eat the freshest sushi in the world.

activities.name: Roppongi Hills & Mori Art Museum
activities.description: One of Tokyo's most impressive urban complexes. The Mori Art Museum on the 53rd floor combines contemporary art with the best observation deck in Tokyo — Tokyo City View.

days.neighborhoods: Yokohama · Minato Mirai · Cup Noodles Museum
days.title: Yokohama Day — Cup Noodles & Chinatown
days.description: Day trip to Yokohama — Japan's second city, just 30 minutes from Tokyo. Visit the Cup Noodles Museum (make your own!), explore the massive Chinatown, and see the gorgeous Minato Mirai waterfront.

activities.name: Cup Noodles Museum
activities.description: The interactive museum celebrating instant noodles inventor Momofuku Ando. The highlight: design your own Cup Noodles package and choose your toppings from scratch.

activities.name: Yokohama Chinatown
activities.description: The largest Chinatown in Japan (and one of the biggest in the world) — over 500 shops and restaurants packed into colorful streets. The food is incredible and the energy is electric. Yokohama's modern waterfront district — skyscrapers, the iconic Cosmo Clock ferris wheel, and gorgeous bay views. Great for a family stroll.

activities.name: Return to Tokyo & Shimokitazawa
activities.description: Head back to Tokyo and explore Shimokitazawa — Tokyo's coolest neighborhood. Vintage shops, live music venues, tiny cafés, and a bohemian vibe completely different from the rest of Tokyo.

days.title: Last Full Day — Hidden Tokyo & Up Garage
days.description: Your final full day in Tokyo. Hit the spots most tourists miss: Nakano Broadway (the real otaku paradise), Up Garage for JDM parts shopping, and one last epic Tokyo night.

activities.name: Nakano Broadway — The Real Akihabara
activities.description: Where serious collectors shop. Four floors of tiny shops selling vintage toys, rare anime figures, retro games, and — crucially — incredible JDM car collectibles that you won't find in touristy Akihabara.

activities.name: 🏎️ Up Garage — JDM Parts Shopping
activities.description: The ultimate used JDM parts chain. Wheels, body kits, exhausts, interior parts — all from real Japanese cars. Even if you can't ship parts home, browsing is incredible. Check multiple locations for the best finds. A massive entertainment complex with an aquarium, planetarium, shopping, and Pokémon Center. Great for families — the Sunshine Aquarium on the rooftop is unique.

activities.name: Shinjuku Golden Gai — Farewell Night Out
activities.description: End your trip at Golden Gai — six narrow alleys of 200+ tiny bars, each seating 6-10 people. Every bar has its own theme and personality. Some welcome tourists, some are regulars-only — look for signs in English.

days.title: Sayonara Japan — Last Bites & Departure
days.description: Your final morning in Japan. Squeeze in last-minute shopping, grab souvenirs, and have one more incredible meal before heading to the airport. You'll be back — everyone comes back.

activities.name: Last Morning Convenience Store Run
activities.description: Japanese convenience stores are a world unto themselves. Stock up on Kit-Kat flavors (matcha, strawberry, sake), Japanese snacks, and unique drinks for the flight home and as gifts. Tokyo Station itself is a destination — the Marunouchi red-brick facade is gorgeous, and the underground shopping areas have every souvenir and treat imaginable.

activities.name: Head to Airport & Fly Home
activities.description: Take the Narita Express (JR Pass) or Limousine Bus to the airport. Check in, browse duty-free for last-minute Japanese whisky or cosmetics, and reflect on 15 incredible days.

editorialSummary: This is the ultimate first-time Japan trip for a family that lives and breathes cars. You'll hunt JDM legends at Daikoku PA, stand where Toyota was born in Nagoya, go-kart through Tokyo's neon streets, and still have time for ancient temples, insane street food, and Golden Week festivals. From the Wangan highway to the bamboo groves of Arashiyama — every day is a new gear.
